source: Per-company AR extraction (Screener.in PDFs + IR sites) — Claude.ai routine, daily batch of 20

china_plus_one.evidence: Zydus MD Sharvil Patel publicly noted that ~60% of medicines consumed in the US are made in India and that US-China trade tensions have opened opportunities for Indian pharma companies like Zydus to capture a larger share of the US generics market as importers seek alternatives to Chinese-linked supply chains; company also emphasizes need to indigenise API/KSM supply chains rather than rely on Chinese intermediates.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 segment mix: US Formulations 35.2% of revenue, International Markets Formulations 13.8%, India Formulations 21.8%, Consumer Wellness 9.6%, Medtech & Others 15.8% (implies ~49% of revenue from US+International export markets).

pli_scheme.evidence: Zydus is cited among leading Gujarat-based API manufacturers (alongside Torrent Pharma, Glenmark Life Sciences) positioned to benefit from India's PLI scheme for APIs/KSMs/drug intermediates aimed at reducing import dependence on China; exact incentive/revenue quantum not confirmed from primary source.

rural.evidence: FY25 commentary highlights volume growth driven by organic expansion and strong performance in Tier-III and Tier-IV towns; network grew to 312 clinical laboratories and 7,727 Patient Service Centres (PSCs), with continued push into smaller towns, though no explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Sona Comstar is a global driveline/EV component supplier with revenue split across North America, Europe, India and RoW (approx. India 25-41%, North America 30-36%, Europe 24-27% across recent quarters). Separately, Sona's MD publicly raised quality concerns over rare earth permanent magnets to be produced domestically under the PLI scheme, reflecting China-dependency risk in the magnet supply chain rather than an explicit China+1 revenue-growth narrative in the AR itself.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company derives roughly half to majority of revenue from North America and Europe combined based on recent quarterly geography splits (e.g. Q2 FY26: India 41%, North America 30%, Europe 24%), implying material USD/EUR revenue exposure, but an FY24-25 full-year figure specifically from the Annual Report could not be confirmed.

pli_scheme.evidence: Sona Comstar is engaged with government on the PLI scheme covering rare earth permanent magnets used in EV motors (its MD raised product-quality concerns over magnets planned to be produced under the scheme), indicating the company's involvement in PLI-linked EV component/magnet manufacturing plans; exact incentive/revenue contribution not disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: IKS Health's care-enablement platform serves 775+ healthcare organizations, predominantly physician enterprises in the US (also Canada and Australia), with delivery centers in India; revenue is overwhelmingly billed in USD from US clients even though an exact disclosed percentage could not be confirmed. FY25 consolidated revenue was ~INR 2,664 crore (up ~47% YoY); FY25/FY26 filings also show recurring net foreign-exchange gains consistent with large USD receivables.

rural.evidence: Radico's distribution network (60,000-100,000+ retail outlets pan-India) is described as emphasizing semi-urban and rural penetration, with growth in IMFL attributed partly to rising disposable incomes and legal-drinking-age population growth in tier-2 cities and rural areas; no explicit rural revenue % disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are grain and molasses used to produce extra neutral alcohol (ENA), not crude oil; FY25 commentary notes a 'relatively stable raw material cost environment' with management watching ENA and grain pricing into FY26. Glass/packaging costs (which do have some crude-linked/energy sensitivity) are also a cost component but no % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Radico exports to 85-100+ countries and brands are sold in 50+ countries, but exports remain a small share of a predominantly India-focused IMFL business; exact export revenue % and hedging policy not found.

rural.evidence: New cold rolling mill positioned to support housing, warehousing and industrial sheds, with emphasis on affordable housing under government schemes such as PMAY; no specific rural revenue % disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Company commentary and analyst narratives cite government-driven infrastructure expansion (railways, roads, gas pipelines, urban housing) as a long-term tailwind for steel volume growth; no explicit % of revenue from govt/infra projects disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are iron ore, iron ore fines, chrome ore, manganese ore and coal (sourced from Odisha Mining Corp, MOIL, Coal India subsidiaries); no crude oil/petroleum-based raw material linkage disclosed, consistent with expectation for a coal/iron-ore based steel and ferro-alloys producer.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company exports to 30+ countries (ferro alloys, stainless steel); export share of turnover reported around 10-11% in recent filings (one third-party estimate cited ~21% for a more recent year, so figure should be treated as approximate).

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports account for only ~6-7% of total revenue (serving Asia and Africa); company states the new Sri City (Andhra Pradesh) manufacturing plant, expected to start production by end-2026, is intended to push export contribution into double digits, positioning India as a larger export/manufacturing hub for LG's global operations. No explicit 'China+1' framing found, but export-led manufacturing diversification narrative is present.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (Asia/Africa) are ~6-7% of revenue; LG India manufactures ~95% of products locally and domestic component/raw-material sourcing is ~55% and rising 2-3pp annually, implying import exposure on the remaining ~45% of inputs, but no explicit hedging policy disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: LG Electronics India is a provisionally selected beneficiary under the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) Scheme for White Goods (air conditioner components), selected in the round-2 cohort of 15 companies with committed investment of ~Rs 1,368 crore, and later among firms upgrading to a higher investment category (~additional Rs 1,217 crore committed).

govt_capex.evidence: EIL is a Government of India-owned EPC/engineering consultancy focused on oil & gas and petrochemicals, serving primarily PSU clients (IOCL, ONGC, BPCL, HPCL etc.). FY25 order book hit an all-time high of ~Rs 11,700 crore (order inflow of Rs 8,214 crore in FY25 vs Rs 3,400 crore in FY24). Company is diversifying beyond oil & gas: non-oil-and-gas sectors (incl. defense MOU with Munitions India Ltd, green energy/bamboo-based refinery at Numaligarh) now contribute 30-35% of the order book, targeting 40%, implying traditional oil & gas PSU capex still drives roughly two-thirds of the order book.

crude_exposure.evidence: Crude oil is not a raw material input for EIL (it is a design/engineering consultancy, not a manufacturer), but its order flow and revenue are indirectly linked to crude oil price cycles via clients' refinery/petrochemical capex decisions; no quantified raw-material exposure applicable.

inr_exposure.evidence: International operations revenue grew 32% YoY to ~Rs 371 crore in FY25, driven by expansion in the Middle East (established Abu Dhabi operations, new Saudi Arabia office to tap hydrocarbon capex); percentage of total consolidated revenue from international operations not reliably determinable from available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: International operations accounted for 54% of total revenue (domestic 46%), with Europe (+22.7% YoY), Canada (+17.5% YoY) and emerging markets (+8.6% YoY) cited as growth drivers, and the company noted 'growth outpacing the industry across all markets.' No explicit China+1/supply-chain-diversification-from-China framing found in available sources, so export growth is noted without a diversification narrative.

rural.evidence: Emcure's established strength in Tier-II and Tier-III Indian cities was cited as a key reason Novo Nordisk chose it as local distribution partner for its semaglutide brand (Poviztra), with plans to make the product accessible across Tier-2/Tier-3 India; company has a domestic field force of 5,000+ personnel. No specific rural revenue % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International/export revenue was 54% of total FY revenue vs. 46% domestic; key export markets are US, Europe, Canada and emerging markets. No specific hedging policy disclosed in available sources.

pli_scheme.evidence: Emcure Pharmaceuticals is one of 9 domestic pharmaceutical companies approved under Group B of the Government of India's PLI Scheme for Pharmaceuticals (Rs 15,000 crore outlay scheme covering 55 selected applicants); revenue contribution from the scheme not separately disclosed.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company MD&A/commentary explicitly states the 'China+1' strategy and global supply chain diversification are enhancing India's role as a trusted global manufacturing hub, and that Divi's is a key Indian beneficiary of global China+1 outsourcing as innovator pharma companies diversify supply chains amid geopolitical risk, BIOSECURE Act concerns and tariffs on Chinese pharma inputs. This is directly tied to custom synthesis/CDMO revenue growth: three dedicated custom-synthesis projects in validation/pre-commercialization (targeted for commercialization in 2027) and a ~Rs 650-750 crore long-term customer-backed capacity agreement (May 2025) described as validation of Divi's growing strategic role in global CDMO supply chains.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports consistently reported at ~85-90% of total sales, with North America and Europe the largest markets and Rest of World the balance (illustrative quarterly splits: Europe ~58% / US ~14% of export revenue in one quarter; Europe+US combined ~73-74% of export sales in another). Product mix roughly 43% generics / 57% custom synthesis. No specific hedging policy disclosed in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports contributed approximately 1% of turnover in FY2024-25; company is overwhelmingly a domestic-market player (electrical + communication cables) with no China+1 / supply-chain diversification narrative found in secondary sources.

rural.evidence: MD&A commentary (via broker/industry summaries) notes Finolex's strategy of tapping rural and semi-urban markets, with rural electrification schemes and 'Make in India' cited as demand drivers for electrical wires, but no specific rural revenue % is disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Growth drivers cited include 100% electrification of the railway network, rural electrification schemes, BharatNet optical fibre rollout, and Smart City projects boosting demand for cables; electrical wires & cables segment is ~85% of total revenue. No explicit % of revenue tied to government/infra capex is disclosed.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company is almost debt-free with net cash position (minimal borrowings, cost of floating debt cited around 8.28% on a small residual balance); no material floating-rate liability disclosed.

crude_exposure.evidence: Key raw materials are copper (continuous cast copper rods, produced in-house at Goa plant) and PVC/polymer compounds used for cable insulation (PVC/XLPE are petrochemical/crude-derived); no quantified % of raw material cost tied to crude-linked inputs was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Exports (foreign currency revenue) were ~1% of FY24-25 turnover, implying minimal direct INR/USD revenue exposure.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Finolex Cables being a PLI (Production Linked Incentive) scheme beneficiary.

china_plus_one.evidence: Company has actively de-risked its fluorspar (key raw material) supply chain away from China via long-term contracts with South African miners and a 25% JV in India's only fluorspar beneficiation company, explicitly to diversify sourcing away from China-dominated supply. CDMO/specialty chemicals exports (anchored by Bayer Crop Science, Corteva Agriscience, Fermion) reflect Western agrochem/pharma majors sourcing fluorochemical intermediates from India rather than China, though the AR framing found in secondary sources emphasizes supply security more than an explicit 'China+1 demand-capture' narrative.

crude_exposure.evidence: Core raw material is fluorspar (a mined mineral, not a direct crude-oil derivative), sourced partly from China-dominated global supply; some fluorochemical/HFC intermediates involve chloromethanes which have petrochemical linkage, but no quantified % of raw material cost tied to crude was found.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export contribution to revenue was 56% in FY25 (down from 65% in FY24); HPP (refrigerant/HFC) business revenue given in INR with USD-linked realisations (e.g. peak revenue potential quoted at USD 5-6.3/kg for new HFC capacity).

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Navin Fluorine participating in a PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Domestic hospital chain; no China+1 / manufacturing supply-chain relevance.

rate_sensitive.evidence: Company has deleveraged significantly; debt-to-equity ratio reduced from 46.6% to 15.8% over the past 5 years, with cash exceeding total debt, indicating low residual interest-rate sensitivity. No specific floating-rate liability % disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: International patient revenue was ~6% of total revenue in Q4FY25 (up 17% YoY to Rs 55.7 cr); 'deemed export of services' (medical tourism/international patients, which earns export incentive treatment) was 5.19% of total turnover in FY2024-25, up from 4.94% in FY2023-24 (per Business Responsibility & Sustainability Report).

pli_scheme.evidence: Not applicable to hospital/healthcare services business; no PLI evidence found.

china_plus_one.evidence: Multiple quantified China import-substitution opportunities cited by analysts drawing on company disclosures: IBCC (Iodobenzyl Cyanide) - India imports ~USD 15-16mn/year entirely from China, with Aether targeting a 25-30% global-volume substitution opportunity and ~10% global market share; DMTA/Memantine intermediate imports (~USD 1-2mn/yr, majority from China) also flagged as a substitution opportunity. Aether markets itself as sole Indian manufacturer of several specialty intermediates previously import-dependent on China, explicitly tying future revenue growth to China-substitution.

crude_exposure.evidence: Business is petrochemical-derived specialty chemical/pharma & agrochem intermediates (advanced intermediates, CRAMS), implying meaningful petrochemical feedstock linkage, but no quantified % of raw material cost tied to crude-linked feedstocks was found in available sources.

inr_exposure.evidence: Export revenue was ~54.5% of total revenue in Q3 FY25 (used as proxy for FY24-25 full-year mix in absence of a full-year disclosure); company exports to ~18 countries including US, Italy, Spain, Germany.

pli_scheme.evidence: No confirmed evidence that Aether Industries is a beneficiary of the PLI (Bulk Drugs/Chemicals) scheme; only general scheme context found, not company-specific confirmation.

china_plus_one.evidence: Caplin is a 100%-export generics company to Latin America (~85% of revenue), Africa and the US, but its own sourcing shows reliance ON China rather than diversification away from it: ~30-40% of outsourced LatAm product supply is sourced from China (balance from in-house/Indian vendors), and the company has explicitly partnered with Chinese pharma companies holding US/EU ANDAs to file products faster in LatAm markets ('China 2.0' partnership strategy). This is the inverse of a China+1 diversification narrative -- it reflects Caplin leveraging Chinese manufacturing relationships rather than displacing China-linked competition.

inr_exposure.evidence: Entire revenue is export-derived (no domestic India sales); ~85% of revenue from LatAm currencies, ~10-18% US (USD), ~6% Africa. Company discloses forex risk exposure: 'adverse currency fluctuations could impact revenue and margin especially as the company derives about 85% of revenue from LatAm.' No specific hedging program disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: No evidence found of Caplin Point participating in a PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Castrol India is an almost entirely domestic-focused lubricants business (revenue overwhelmingly from India); no export/China+1 diversification narrative found in coverage of FY25 results.

rural.evidence: Rural distribution expanded to ~40,000 outlets supported by ~500 Rural Service Express centres; management described the rural portfolio as growing at a 'high double-digit rate' and cited rural expansion as a key driver of FY25's record revenue (Castrol India FY25 results coverage, Autocar Professional / Motorindia / S&P Global Aftermarket Insight).

crude_exposure.evidence: Base oil and additives (crude-oil derivatives) are Castrol India's primary raw materials; roughly 50-55% of base oil is imported. Analyst commentary notes margins move inversely with crude/base-oil prices (e.g., a $25/tonne rise in raw material prices was estimated to cut EPS ~3%), and FY25 cost relief from softer crude was partly offset by a weaker rupee (ICICI Direct / Business Standard coverage).

inr_exposure.evidence: No material USD-denominated revenue disclosed (business is domestic); rupee movements affect Castrol mainly via the cost side (imported base oil), not export revenue.

china_plus_one.evidence: International markets accounted for ~55% of FY25 consolidated revenue (₹3,474 cr total, up 7.7% YoY), attributed to 'sustained demand in sectors such as oil and gas, mining, and infrastructure.' No explicit China+1 / supply-chain-diversification framing was found in available coverage.

govt_capex.evidence: Wire Rope segment (72% of FY25 revenue) serves mining, infrastructure, and oil & offshore end-markets; management cited infrastructure and mining demand as growth drivers, but no specific govt-capex revenue percentage disclosed.

inr_exposure.evidence: Company has significant export revenue (~55% international in FY25) implying meaningful multi-currency exposure, but no specific USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy was disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI Scheme for Specialty Steel has drawn ~75 applicants including Tata Steel, JSW Steel, JSPL, AMNS India and SAIL; Usha Martin was not identified as a confirmed beneficiary in available sources.

china_plus_one.evidence: Foreign exchange earnings reportedly grew to ~₹300 crore from ~₹100 crore over five years, with company expanding exports (batteries, incl. defence batteries) to the Middle East, APAC, Africa and Europe. No explicit China+1/diversification framing found; export growth appears driven by company's own defence/industrial battery order wins rather than customer de-risking from China.

govt_capex.evidence: Electronics segment (Rail Signalling, Kavach, TMS/CTC) is heavily government/railway-order driven; segment reported to have grown from ~15% of revenue in FY25 to ~49% in FY26, with Kavach ~50% of electronics sales. Company also supplies defence batteries and electronic fuzes with claimed 100% indigenisation, tied to defence/railway capex cycles (CARE Ratings press releases, company commentary).

pli_scheme.evidence: HBL Engineering is not among the four firms (Reliance New Energy Solar, Ola Electric Mobility, Hyundai Global Motors, Rajesh Exports) selected as beneficiaries under India's ACC Battery Storage PLI scheme.

china_plus_one.evidence: Exports account for ~20% of total sales volume across ~30 countries; company is diversifying its own manufacturing footprint (Dubai plant) and targets international sales >1 MMT. This reflects the company's own geographic expansion strategy rather than a customer-driven China+1/de-risking narrative.

rural.evidence: PMAY-Gramin (rural housing scheme) extended to FY29, targeting 2 crore additional rural houses; cited as a demand tailwind for structural steel tube/pipe volumes, though no specific rural revenue percentage is disclosed.

govt_capex.evidence: Approximately 64% of revenue comes from the housing/residential sector (incl. PMAY-Urban 2.0 targeting 1 crore urban houses); management also flagged the government's proposed ₹12.2 lakh crore infrastructure capex push for FY26-27 as a tailwind for structural steel demand. Note: the 64% figure covers housing/residential broadly (private + government-scheme-driven), not government capex alone.

crude_exposure.evidence: Primary raw materials are HR steel coils, galvanized coils and zinc (steel-linked), not crude oil derivatives; company sources >80% of HRC from Tata Steel and JSW Steel, giving a procurement cost edge.

china_plus_one.evidence: No Torrent-specific China+1 narrative found. Broader industry context notes India imports 53+ critical pharma APIs from China and that PLI aims to reduce this dependency, but this was not tied specifically to Torrent Pharma's own revenue/order growth in sources reviewed.

inr_exposure.evidence: FY25 revenue geography: India ~55%, Brazil ~10%, US ~10%, Germany ~10%, other markets ~15% (Torrent ranked No.1 among Indian pharma companies in Brazil and Germany); ~45% of revenue is international, implying multi-currency (USD/EUR/BRL) exposure, but no specific USD-revenue percentage or hedging policy was disclosed in sources reviewed.

pli_scheme.evidence: India's PLI scheme for bulk drugs/KSMs (e.g., Penicillin G) exists industry-wide, but Torrent Pharmaceuticals was not identified as a confirmed beneficiary in sources reviewed.
